verdict.rationale: Cloudflare positions Workers as serverless with no servers, cold starts, region complexity or capacity planning, and with the same bindings, Durable Objects-backed agents and data primitives used from `npm create cloudflare` onward. The Agents SDK is documented as scaling to tens of millions of instances on the same code. A community user reports going from zero to a production API in an hour, which supports the prototype end of the story. However, another user notes that per-request CPU-time limits (30s free, 15min paid) don't fit long-running workloads, which could force a shift to other primitives such as Workflows or Containers. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of a no-rearchitecture path from free tier to large scale, and independent or hands-on corroboration of apps scaling massively on unchanged primitives.
